title: How Often Should You Replace a Whole-House Water Filter?

seo.title: How Often Should You Replace a Whole-House Water Filter?
seo.meta_description: There is no single replacement interval for every whole-house water filter.
seo.search_intent: Determine how often to replace a whole-house water filter using manufacturer limits, water quality, household use, and signs of flow restriction.

excerpt: There is no single replacement interval for every whole-house water filter. Cartridge type, incoming water quality, household use, and pressure drop determine whether replacement is based on time, capacity, or performance.
content_html:
There is no single replacement interval for every whole-house water filter. Cartridge type, incoming water quality, household use, and pressure drop determine whether replacement is based on time, capacity, or performance.

Start with the manufacturer’s limit and filter type

A sediment prefilter may need replacement much more often than a large-capacity carbon stage. Record the installation date and exact part number so you do not apply an interval intended for a different system.

Household pressure drop is a useful clue

If showers and faucets lose flow throughout the home while incoming supply is otherwise normal, a loaded filter may be adding restriction. Check valves and other possible bottlenecks before assuming the cartridge is the only cause.

High sediment loads shorten filter life

Utility work, sediment-heavy wells, or older piping can load a prefilter before the calendar date. If cartridges clog repeatedly in a short time, investigate the source rather than simply replacing filters more often.

Do not stretch service life just to avoid replacement

An exhausted filter can lose treatment performance, while a heavily clogged one can reduce pressure. Follow manufacturer limits and, when the system targets specific contaminants, use replacement media that maintains the required certification.
